extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of political theory, constitutional law, and intellectual history (educated general readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Close-reading and critique of Montesquieu's principal doctrines (separation of powers, mixed government, penal and social reforms) as presented in a scholarly overview. The page supplies normative principles and argumentative guidance about constitutional design, criminal law, slavery, tolerance, and social policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of powers as condition of liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: «La base de la théorie de Montesquieu n'est pas la distinction des gouvernements, mais la distinction des pouvoirs; non pas la combinaison des trois formes de gouvernement, mais la séparation des trois pouvoirs. ... Les trois pouvoirs sont-ils réunis, c'est le despotisme; séparés, c'est la liberté.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat separation of legislative, executive and judicial powers as the fundamental constitutional principle securing freedom. The text explains that combining powers leads to despotism and separation to liberty; this is the core evaluative standard for judging whether a constitution is 'libre'. Examples and caveats follow (see independence of judiciary, necessary interdependence for action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish types of government from kinds of powers
rubrics_metrics.description: «Il y a trois sortes de gouvernements, et il y a trois sortes de pouvoirs dans le gouvernement: ce sont deux choses très différentes.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate 'government form' (republic, aristocracy, monarchy) with the 'powers' (legislative, executive, judicial). A constitution may be a simple government yet have separated powers (e.g., United States) or be mixed yet have powers combined (ancient Rome). Evaluations should separately assess form and distribution of powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute independence of the judiciary
rubrics_metrics.description: «Que le pouvoir judiciaire doive être nécessairement indépendant, c'est ce qui saute d'abord aux yeux de tout le monde. ... 'Si la puissance de juger était jointe à la législative, le pouvoir sur la vie et la liberté des citoyens serait arbitraire, car le juge serait législateur; si elle était jointe à la puissance exécutrice, le juge pourrait avoir la force d'un oppresseur.'»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge constitutional designs by whether the judicial power is insulated from legislative and executive control. Independence of the judiciary is presented as an essential, nearly non-negotiable guarantee against arbitrariness and oppression; anti-patterns include judges who make law or exercise executive force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of executive and legislative powers
rubrics_metrics.description: «Mais est-il nécessaire que le pouvoir exécutif soit séparé du législatif? Il le faut sans doute; car, si celui qui a la force fait les lois, qui peut l'empêcher de les faire comme il l'entend, c'est-à-dire tyranniques et oppressives? ...»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitute executive and legislative powers separately so that the body possessing physical force cannot unilaterally make laws. Evaluation should check for mechanisms preventing the executive (or the legislature) from using armed force to implement arbitrary legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits to popular exercise of concentrated power
rubrics_metrics.description: «Le peuple, à titre de souverain, doit avoir à la fois le pouvoir exécutif et le pouvoir législatif, et il est impossible qu'il en abuse... Je réponds que le peuple peut certainement être injuste et oppresseur... 'Il ne faut pas confondre le pouvoir du peuple avec la liberté du peuple'.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even majority-rule (popular sovereignty) needs institutional limits: the people should not directly and simultaneously exercise both executive and legislative power. Assessment should consider whether institutions prevent majority tyranny against minorities or particular interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary interdependence and checks (not pure isolation)
rubrics_metrics.description: «De plus, il ne suffit pas de séparer les pouvoirs, il faut les unir et les accorder. ... La nécessité même de l'indépendance des pouvoirs exige que chacun ait une certaine part dans l'action de l'autre. Si le pouvoir législatif ne peut rien sur l'exécutif, celui-ci rendra le premier tout à fait vain; si l'exécutif ne peut rien sur le législatif, celui-ci s'emparera de l'exécutif.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate constitutions for a balance between separation and functional cooperation: institutional checks where each power has limited influence over others to ensure both independence and capacity for action. Pure isolation (no overlap) is criticized as impractical; anti-patterns include designs that make one branch impotent or absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation reduces but does not eliminate abuse; public opinion as safeguard
rubrics_metrics.description: «Le principe de la séparation des pouvoirs n'a pas cette portée ni cette efficacité. Il empêche certains abus, mais non pas tous les abus... D'ailleurs, dans un pays constitué de cette manière, il y a toujours en dehors des pouvoirs publics un pouvoir moral, invisible... c'est l'opinion. Or l'opinion exprimée par la presse, voilà la dernière garantie de la liberté...»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing protections against tyranny, recognize limits of institutional design: separation mitigates specific abuses but cannot stop collusion among powers. Complementary safeguards (free press, public opinion, civil society) are critical. Anti-pattern: relying solely on constitutional separation without independent social institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberation and resistance are political goods
rubrics_metrics.description: «Le ralentissement dans les affaires humaines, ce n'est pas un mal, c'est un bien: car c'est la réflexion, le sang-froid, l'examen, par conséquent beaucoup de chances pour la vérité, et beaucoup contre l'erreur.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value institutional frictions (checks, delays, mutual resistance) as means of reasoned decision-making and error prevention. Design evaluations should not penalize slow processes per se; instead, recognize their role in preserving liberty and preventing hasty tyranny. Anti-pattern: equating speed with good governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-government ideal (monarchy/aristocracy/people) is context-dependent
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of Montesquieu's second theory: executive (monarch), legislative (people), and nobility as mediator — and the question whether genuine aristocracy (with privilege) is necessary for liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying the 'mixed government' rubric, distinguish idealized historical models from practical applicability: do not assume an aristocracy with hereditary privileges is required for liberty in modern societies. Evaluate whether the elements (monarchy, aristocracy, democracy) are present literally, analogically, or absent; beware of forcing historical labels onto contemporary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation and humanity in criminal penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: «La sévérité... convient plus au gouvernement despotique... Dans les bons gouvernements, il vaut mieux prévenir que punir, et en punissant employer une certaine douceur, plus analogue au principe du gouvernement. La sévérité des peines est contraire à la liberté, et avec la liberté les peines s'adoucissent.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal law should favor prevention, proportionality and milder punishments in free regimes. Evaluate penal codes for excessive severity, disproportionate punishments, and remnants of medieval cruelty. Anti-patterns include extreme penalties that desensitize the population and corrode the state's moral legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolition of torture and cruel punishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Text notes Montesquieu's brief but pointed attack on torture: he implies torture is unnecessary and marks it as associated with despotism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess legal systems for use or toleration of torture and barbarous punishments. The standard is abolition or severe restriction; recognizing that Montesquieu framed torture as a despotism-associated instrument and argued against it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of slavery as incompatible with natural liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: Montesquieu's arguments against slavery: no necessity justifies enslaving prisoners; sale of persons is incoherent ('La vente suppose un prix... l'esclave ne recevrait rien...'); 'la liberté de chaque citoyen est une partie de la liberté publique.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat slavery or legal servitude as a fundamental injustice and a violation of the public liberty. Evaluation should consider legal prohibitions on slavery and critique justifications like war-prize or contract. Anti-patterns: laws that systemically advantage ruling classes and make law 'always against' the oppressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious toleration as political and moral necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: «Tolérer une religion, dit-il, ce n'est pas l'approuver. ... Dans un État qui repose sur l'unité et la paix, s'il y a plusieurs religions, il faut qu'elles se tolèrent... Car il ne suffit pas qu'un citoyen n'agite pas l'État, il faut encore qu'il ne trouble pas un autre citoyen.'»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess policies on religion by whether they secure peaceful coexistence and forbid coercive conversion or persecution. Toleration is required for state unity; anti-patterns include using religion as an instrument of repression (auto-da-fés, persecutions) that destabilize the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: State duty to secure subsistence via work and education (limited welfare principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: «Un État bien policé tire cette subsistance du fond des arts mêmes: il donne aux uns les travaux dont ils sont capables, il enseigne aux autres à travailler... 'Un État doit à tous les citoyens une subsistance assurée, la nourriture, un vêtement convenable et un genre de vie qui ne soit pas contraire à la santé.'» (note: the footnote remarks this principle is 'dangerous' and Montesquieu did not foresee all consequences.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard for social policy: the state should secure subsistence not by unstructured alms but by promoting work, distributing suitable employment, and teaching skills. Evaluation should weigh prudence and feasibility; beware of interpreting this as an absolute entitlement without considering economic consequences (the page notes potential dangers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Penal reform legacy: punish without demeaning humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: Montesquieu credited with initiating reforms that led to modern penal laws 'qui répriment sans avilir, qui punissent sans opprimer, qui enfin ne troublent pas le sentiment de la justice en blessant celui de l'humanité.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging penal systems, prioritize reforms that maintain dignity, avoid dehumanizing punishments, and align sanctions with moral sensibility. Use Montesquieu's legacy as a benchmark for humane legislative change in criminal justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of irony and rhetorical strategy in political critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Montesquieu used irony and poignant rhetoric (e.g., on the sugar trade and condition of Africans) to attack entrenched institutions like slavery and the slave trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating political argumentation, consider not only logical arguments but rhetorical strategies (irony, moral appeal) that can be effective in changing public opinion and policy. The page highlights how rhetorical force complemented philosophical argument in effecting social reform.
